Done. Everything is in one file: `app/src/main/java/com/trianguloy/urlchecker/modules/list/UriPartsModule.java`.

## Root cause

The module parsed query parameters with `android.net.UrlQuerySanitizer`, which has two defects that compound:

1. **`UrlQuerySanitizer.unescape()` decodes as Latin-1, not UTF-8** — it turns each `%XX` escape into a single `char` (`(char) byteValue`), so a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence like `%E6%9D%A5` (来) becomes three garbage chars `æ`, `` , `¥` instead of one character.
2. **It was fed `uri.getQuery()`, which is already decoded** — so the query was decoded *twice*: correctly by `Uri` first, then incorrectly by the sanitizer. Splitting already-decoded text on `&`/`=` is also unsafe, since separators encoded inside a value (`?u=a%26b%3Dc`) would split into extra bogus parameters.

That's exactly the reported trace: raw `prefill_%25E6%259D%25A5…` → `getQuery()` → `prefill_%E6%9D%A5…` → sanitizer's Latin-1 unescape → `prefill_æ¥æº`. Then `Uri.Builder.appendQueryParameter()` re-encoded that mojibake as UTF-8, doubling the corruption into `%C3%A6%C2%9D%C2%A5…` and breaking the URL.

## Fix

Dropped `UrlQuerySanitizer` and replaced it with two small helpers:

- **`splitEncodedQuery(uri.getEncodedQuery())`** — splits the *still-encoded* query on `&`, then on the first `=` only, so encoded separators inside values can never split a parameter. Empty parameters (`&&`) are skipped as before.
- **`decode(...)`** — decodes percent-escapes as UTF-8 via `URLDecoder.decode(s, "UTF-8")`, repeating while the text keeps changing (to handle the multiply-encoded `%25E6…` case), and keeping the last valid result on failure. This is deliberately more forgiving than `Uri.decode()`, which would replace invalid escapes with `�`; a malformed value like `100%` or `%zz` is now displayed verbatim instead of being mangled or throwing.

The surrounding structure — decode for display, rebuild via `appendQueryParameter` when deleting — is left untouched, since that normalize-on-delete behavior was the module's existing design.

## Verification

Build passes (`./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL). I also ran the extracted logic standalone against the reported URL and edge cases:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Reported URL, display | `prefill_来源 -> 帮助与反馈` ✅ matches expected |
| Reported URL, remove `hide` | `https://example.com?prefill_%E6%9D%A5%E6%BA%90=%E5%B8%AE%E5%8A%A9%E4%B8%8E%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88` ✅ matches expected |
| Normal single-encoded UTF-8 | round-trips unchanged (idempotent) |
| `?u=a%26b%3Dc` | stays **one** parameter `u -> a&b=c` (previously split in two) |
| `flag` (no `=`), `empty=`, `a+b`, `100%`, `%zz` | no crash, no `�`, malformed escapes shown as-is |
| Duplicate names `a=1&a=2` | both listed, correct one removed |

One judgement call worth flagging: I made `decode` repeat until stable so the doubly-encoded name collapses to `prefill_来源` and the rebuilt URL matches the report's "Expected URL" exactly. The stricter alternative — decoding exactly once and preserving each parameter byte-for-byte on delete — would instead display `prefill_%E6%9D%A5%E6%BA%90` and keep `%25E6…` in the URL. That is arguably the more literal reading of the URL, but it contradicts both "Expected" lines in the report, so I followed the report. Repeated decoding is a no-op for normal single-encoded URLs (verified above), so it only affects multiply-encoded parameters.

extra.final_message:
Done. Everything is in one file: `app/src/main/java/com/trianguloy/urlchecker/modules/list/UriPartsModule.java`.

## Root cause

The module parsed query parameters with `android.net.UrlQuerySanitizer`, which has two defects that compound:

1. **`UrlQuerySanitizer.unescape()` decodes as Latin-1, not UTF-8** — it turns each `%XX` escape into a single `char` (`(char) byteValue`), so a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence like `%E6%9D%A5` (来) becomes three garbage chars `æ`, `` , `¥` instead of one character.
2. **It was fed `uri.getQuery()`, which is already decoded** — so the query was decoded *twice*: correctly by `Uri` first, then incorrectly by the sanitizer. Splitting already-decoded text on `&`/`=` is also unsafe, since separators encoded inside a value (`?u=a%26b%3Dc`) would split into extra bogus parameters.

That's exactly the reported trace: raw `prefill_%25E6%259D%25A5…` → `getQuery()` → `prefill_%E6%9D%A5…` → sanitizer's Latin-1 unescape → `prefill_æ¥æº`. Then `Uri.Builder.appendQueryParameter()` re-encoded that mojibake as UTF-8, doubling the corruption into `%C3%A6%C2%9D%C2%A5…` and breaking the URL.

## Fix

Dropped `UrlQuerySanitizer` and replaced it with two small helpers:

- **`splitEncodedQuery(uri.getEncodedQuery())`** — splits the *still-encoded* query on `&`, then on the first `=` only, so encoded separators inside values can never split a parameter. Empty parameters (`&&`) are skipped as before.
- **`decode(...)`** — decodes percent-escapes as UTF-8 via `URLDecoder.decode(s, "UTF-8")`, repeating while the text keeps changing (to handle the multiply-encoded `%25E6…` case), and keeping the last valid result on failure. This is deliberately more forgiving than `Uri.decode()`, which would replace invalid escapes with `�`; a malformed value like `100%` or `%zz` is now displayed verbatim instead of being mangled or throwing.

The surrounding structure — decode for display, rebuild via `appendQueryParameter` when deleting — is left untouched, since that normalize-on-delete behavior was the module's existing design.

## Verification

Build passes (`./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL). I also ran the extracted logic standalone against the reported URL and edge cases:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Reported URL, display | `prefill_来源 -> 帮助与反馈` ✅ matches expected |
| Reported URL, remove `hide` | `https://example.com?prefill_%E6%9D%A5%E6%BA%90=%E5%B8%AE%E5%8A%A9%E4%B8%8E%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88` ✅ matches expected |
| Normal single-encoded UTF-8 | round-trips unchanged (idempotent) |
| `?u=a%26b%3Dc` | stays **one** parameter `u -> a&b=c` (previously split in two) |
| `flag` (no `=`), `empty=`, `a+b`, `100%`, `%zz` | no crash, no `�`, malformed escapes shown as-is |
| Duplicate names `a=1&a=2` | both listed, correct one removed |

One judgement call worth flagging: I made `decode` repeat until stable so the doubly-encoded name collapses to `prefill_来源` and the rebuilt URL matches the report's "Expected URL" exactly. The stricter alternative — decoding exactly once and preserving each parameter byte-for-byte on delete — would instead display `prefill_%E6%9D%A5%E6%BA%90` and keep `%25E6…` in the URL. That is arguably the more literal reading of the URL, but it contradicts both "Expected" lines in the report, so I followed the report. Repeated decoding is a no-op for normal single-encoded URLs (verified above), so it only affects multiply-encoded parameters.
